specs.note: same in Canada and the U.S.

steps: Unpack & free the barrier screen

Lift the top plate straight off. The barrier screen is fastened to the shipping pallet: remove the two screws and break the perforated shipping straps off both brackets with pliers. It must be installed before the stove is operated.

To open the firebox, disengage the two glass frame latches on top of the firebox: pull each handle forward to clear the latch from the notch in the frame.

Hardware bag

Fuel Conversion Kit - LP155351
Ember Bag, 4 oz.129123
Rock Wool, 1 oz.157259

Read the installation requirements before starting. Wear gloves and safety glasses while installing.
Location & floor protection

Never directly on carpeting, vinyl, linoleum or Pergo®. On any combustible floor other than wood, install a metal, wood, ceramic, stone or listed hearth pad covering the full width and depth of the stove.

Weigh heat distribution, vent termination, gas supply line routing, and traffic areas, furniture and draperies. Leave access around the stove for service. Carpeting, vinyl or linoleum doesn't have to be removed from under the floor protection. The minimum hearth protection is shown as a diagram (Fig. 1).

Hold the clearances to combustibles on p. 7. "Fire resistant" materials and "fire-rated" sheet rock are considered combustible.
Vent system & restrictors

Use one approved maker's vent parts throughout and seal each inner-pipe joint with a 1/8" bead of high-temperature (750°F) sealant, never silicone. Set the exhaust restrictor for the termination zone; open the intake restrictor only where called for.

Approved: M&G DuraVent (Direct Vent Pro Series), Metal-Fab Sure-Seal DV, Amerivent, Security Vent, Selkirk Metalbestos, International Chimney Corp. (ExcelDirect), Bernard Delsin (Pro Form), Olympia Chimney Supply (Ventis Direct Vent). Don't mix makers, modify components or use damaged venting. The stove needs its own vent system, vented directly outside; common vents are prohibited.

Intake air restrictor

At the rear of the firebox behind the burner plate; set CLOSED at the factory. Open it only for snorkel terminations and some short horizontal runs (on propane, terminations 5 ft and under): loosen the wing nut under the burner and push it back as far as it will go (Fig. 6, p. 9).

Exhaust restrictor

Shutter at the top of the firebox with four pivot-pin positions; set FULLY OPEN at the factory. Use the position letter of the termination zone in the vent windows (Figs. 9–12, pp. 10–11): NG co-linear B; LP straight vertical co-linear C; LP vertical co-linear with maximum 2 ft. offset A. To adjust: remove the top plate, loosen the wing nut on the pivot pin at the left of the firebox top, push the pin left, move it toward the rear and then right into the marked position, tighten, refit the top plate. Tall vents may need Simpson Dura-Vent Restrictor Disk #929.
Mobile home: secure & ground

Secure the stove to the floor with Jøtul Floor Bracket Kit #750304 and provide an electrical ground between the stove and the chassis. Install to Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 in the U.S., or CSA Z240.4 in Canada.
Approved for an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured (mobile) home where not prohibited by local codes. Always contact local officials about restrictions and requirements in your area.
Fuel conversion (if propane)

Done by an authorized service technician, before the stove is installed: change the burner orifice (1.65 mm LP) and pilot orifice (#30 LP), fit the propane regulator tower, apply the labels, then leak-test.

1. Turn off the gas. Remove the top plate, the glass panel (two latches), any embers and logs, and the burner skirt.
  2. Remove the air shutter wingnut under the stove (right side, the one closest to you). Pull the shutter forward and lift the burner plate and shutter out as a unit; the burner isn't screwed down.
  3. Change the main burner orifice with a 1/2" open ended wrench or deep-well socket: #33 NG, 1.65 mm LP.
  4. Refit the air shutter with its gasket, pushed all the way back, then the burner plate: engage the air inlet tube with the shutter and orifice, and the front corners with the two support brackets. Leave the wingnut loose.
  5. Pull the pilot head straight up. With the 4 mm allen wrench, change the pilot orifice (#51 NG, #30 LP); tighten it flush with the base to prevent bypass leaks, then push the head back on.
  6. With a Torx T-20, remove the three regulator screws, then the tower, gasket, white plastic disk and spring. Fit the new regulator with its gasket positioned; tighten the screws securely.
  7. Apply Label A (back of stove), Label B (rating plate) and the small valve label (valve). Reassemble, apply gas and leak-test with soapy water.
  8. Adjust the air shutter last: start with the stem midway in the slot; back restricts air, forward opens the shutter.
Gas connection + leak test

Connect a 3/8" npt line with 1/2" diameter supply to the left side of the valve, with a shut-off valve (T-handle in Massachusetts) and union in the same room. Leak-test with soapy water, never an open flame.

The line should be 3/8" npt with a 1/2" diameter supply, or the size needed to provide sufficient gas pressure to the valve regardless of the input setting. Connect it before installing the optional blower, using an elbow off the control valve to create clearance for it.

Note: p. 17 says to use a 45° elbow off the control valve to create clearance for the blower; p. 24 says to use a 90° elbow.

Use propane-resistant sealing compounds on propane units. Flexible gas appliance connectors are acceptable in many areas in the U.S.; Canadian methods vary with local code. Disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve during supply-piping tests in excess of 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa), and isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve during tests equal to or exceeding 1/2 psig.

Leak test

  1. Mix a 50-50 solution of water and dish soap.
  2. Light the appliance.
  3. Brush or spray all joints and connections.
  4. Bubbles or a gas odor: turn the gas control knob to OFF, tighten or reconnect the joint, and retest.
Check gas pressures
Attach a manometer to the test points on the front of the valve, under the On/Off/Pilot knob: E for inlet (supply), A for manifold. Always test with the valve control knob set on HIGH.

NG inlet5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
LP inlet12.0 – 14.9 in. WC
NG manifold1.2 – 3.8 in. WC
LP manifold2.9 – 11.0 in. WC

Correct pressure must be established at the time of installation. No altitude adjustment from 2000 - 4500 ft. (610 m -1370 m); do not derate this appliance for altitude.
Thermostat or remote (optional)

Use only a 750 millivolt DC two-wire thermostat, in the same room, typically 5 feet off the floor. Run at least 16 gauge wire, 25 feet max, to the two lower terminals of the block above the ignitor button; wire a remote receiver the same way.

Don't overtighten the connections; no other wires need disconnecting. For thermostat operation the On/Off/T-Stat switch on the back of the stove must be at T-STAT and the pilot must be running, since it powers the thermostat. Keep the thermostat out of drafty areas.

Label all wires before disconnecting them when servicing the controls. Wiring errors can cause improper or dangerous operation; always verify proper operation after servicing.

Accessories: Wall Thermostat 750003, Remote Control 750002.
Log set & ember stones

Wearing gloves, set the five logs on their locator pins in the order of Figs. 32–37: right, rear, left, middle, crossover. Spread ember stones over the burner plate and around the logs, clear of the pilot assembly, burner skirt openings and carry-over ports.

Install the optional Antique Brick Panel Kit (155375) first, if used. The log set must be installed before operating the burner. You don't need to use all the ember stones; too many can promote sooting on the logs, so adjust the quantity for the best flame picture.
System check & air shutter

Purge air from the gas line on first lighting. The pilot should be steady, blue at the hood with traces of yellow, engulfing the top 3/8" of the thermopile and top 1/8" of the thermocouple. No smoke or soot: check log placement, then the air shutter.

View the pilot through the port at the rear of the right log. It should project 1" out of all three pilot hood ports and over to the burner plate carry-over ports. Don't alter the flame by setting the gas valve control anywhere but full ON; flame height adjusts approximately 1" to 2" between LOW and HIGH with the HI/LOW knob.

Air shutter

Shipped set half-open for natural gas. Reach under the right side and loosen the wingnut closest to you; slide the stem forward to open the shutter (more air) or back to reduce air, then tighten. Run on HIGH for 30 minutes watching the flame; if it looks weak, slow or sooty, open the shutter in small increments and let the burner settle. The more offsets in the vent, the greater the need for adjustment.

Air shutter adjustments should only be performed by a qualified professional service technician.

panels.title: Soot, smoke or long yellow flames
items: Too little combustion air → very long yellow flames, soot on the logs, firebox walls and termination cap
Logs out of place → soot or smoke (check log placement first)
Too many ember stones → sooting on the logs
Weak, slow or sooty after 30 min on HIGH → open the air shutter in small increments

panels.title: Blue or "anemic" flame
items: Too much air at the air shutter → blue, transparent flame
Overly strong draft → poor combustion and weak flame picture (set the restrictor plates)

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: Goes out when the knob is released → repeat lighting steps 5 through 8
Still won't stay lit after several tries → knob to OFF, call a service technician or gas supplier
Knob doesn't spring back → stop and call a service technician or gas supplier
Knob won't push in or turn by hand → don't force or repair it; call a qualified technician

panels.title: Poor draft or down-draft
items: Steep roofs, nearby trees, predominantly windy conditions → poor draft or down-draft; a taller vent may help
Atmospheric pressure, strong prevailing winds, adjacent structures, snow accumulation → reduced performance
More offsets in the vent → greater need for air shutter adjustment

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
Your stove has a standing pilot that you light by hand with the red spark button. Follow these steps exactly. They're also on the stove's rating plate.

Before lighting, smell all around the stove for gas, including next to the floor: some gas is heavier than air. Use only your hand on the control knob, never tools.

  1. Stop and read the safety information.
  2. Set the burner switch to OFF (or a thermostat, if used, to its lowest setting).
  3. Make sure the gas supply shut-off valve is open.
  4. Push the valve control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
  5. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. If you then smell gas, stop (see Safety).
  6. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counter-clockwise to PILOT.
  7. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Press the red button repeatedly until the pilot lights. Keep holding about one minute, then release. The knob should spring back and the pilot stay lit. If it goes out, repeat steps 5 through 8.
  8. Turn the knob counter-clockwise to ON.
  9. Set the burner switch to ON, or the thermostat to the temperature you want.
Call your service technician or gas supplier if the knob doesn't spring back, or if the pilot won't stay lit after several tries (turn the knob to OFF first).
Note: p. 3 and p. 22 say the rating plate is on the back of the stove; p. 21 says it is attached to the bottom of the stove.

controls.title: Turning it on & off
controls.html:
Once the pilot is lit, the burner is controlled by the rocker switch at the left rear corner of the stove.

ONburner on
OFFburner off; the pilot stays lit
T-STATfor an optional wall thermostat or remote

Flame height

Turn the HI/LOW knob in the center of the valve face. The flame changes about 1" to 2" between LOW and HIGH. Leave the valve control knob fully at ON while the stove runs; don't use it to change the flame.

Shutting the gas off completely

Set the burner switch to OFF, then push the valve control knob in and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.

This stove has a continuously burning pilot flame. Take care when using products that give off combustible vapors, and always shut off the gas supply while the stove is being serviced.

firstfire.title: First fires: odor, smoke & foggy glass
firstfire.html:
During the first few fires you may notice an odor or some smoke from the stove. That's normal: manufacturing residue is burning off and materials are curing. Extra ventilation and fresh air help.

Foggy glass

Condensation may form on the glass each time you light the stove. This "fog" disappears as the stove heats up.

The very first lighting

  • It takes a few moments for air to clear out of the gas line. Later starts don't need this unless the gas supply line was shut off.
  • The log set must be in place before the burner is used, and the safety barrier screen before the stove is operated.
Smoke or soot that doesn't go away isn't normal. The log placement should be checked first. If it persists, the air shutter may need adjusting by a qualified professional service technician.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when it needs it, and only when it's cold.

  1. Wipe the surface with a clean, damp, soft cloth.
  2. Follow with a dry, soft towel.
  3. Take care not to scratch the glass.
Never use abrasive cleaners, and never clean the glass while it's hot.

Look for scratches

Scratches can weaken the glass panel. If you find any, have the panel replaced by a licensed or qualified service person, using only Jøtul ceramic glass panel 155553.

  • Never run the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • The glass may shatter unexpectedly if struck. Don't slam or strike it.
  • The glass gasket should be inspected at least once a year.

flame.title: What the flame should look like
flame.html:
The pilot

You can watch the pilot through the view port at the rear of the right log. It should be steady, not lifting or floating, and blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow toward the outer edges.

The fire

Most people enjoy a warm, yellowish flame. Flame height changes about 1" to 2" between the LOW and HIGH settings. There should be no smoke or soot.

Blue and see-through ("anemic")too much air
Very long yellow flames, soottoo little air

Soot shows up as black deposits on the logs, on the inside walls of the stove and possibly on the outside vent cap. Too many ember stones can also cause soot on the logs.

Leave adjustments to a pro. If you see soot or smoke, have the log placement checked. Air shutter adjustments should only be done by a qualified professional service technician.

thermostat.title: Wall thermostat or remote
thermostat.html:
A wall thermostat (Jøtul 750003) and a remote control (750002) are optional accessories. Either one connects to the stove's terminal block.

  • Set the rocker switch at the left rear of the stove to T-STAT.
  • Keep the pilot lit. It is the power source for the thermostat.
  • When you light the stove, set the thermostat to its lowest setting first. Once it's lit, set the temperature you want.
  • For a remote, follow the operating instructions that come with it.

The thermostat belongs in the same room as the stove, typically 5 feet off the floor, away from drafty areas or anything else that could affect its accuracy.

blower.title: The optional blower
blower.html:
The optional variable-speed blower (kit 156000) moves heat around the firebox and out into the room.

AUTOa heat-activated switch starts the blower after the fire has burned for a while, and shuts it off when the stove cools down after the burner turns off
MANUALfor when you don't want automatic circulation
Speed knobsets the fan speed

The blower has a three-prong grounding plug. Plug it directly into a properly grounded three-prong outlet, and never cut or remove the grounding prong.

Before any service, unplug the blower and turn off the gas supply to the stove.

service.title: Yearly check-up
service.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the stove and its venting system before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpeting, bedding and the like can mean more frequent cleaning.

What gets checked

  • The entire vent system, including the chimney, is inspected and cleaned.
  • The firebox is vacuumed with a soft brush. The logs are fragile.
  • The pilot head and its sensors (thermopile and thermocouple) are checked for rust or wear.
  • The burner ports are checked for blockages, especially around the pilot.
  • The glass gasket is checked for wear and a good seal.
  • The firebox, valve compartment, air passages and blower are checked so air can flow freely.

Between visits

Keep the controls and the area under the stove free of debris, and vacuum there often, only when the stove is cold. Keep the area clear of anything that can burn, including gasoline and other flammable liquids.

Before any service, turn off the gas supply and unplug the blower.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
• The stove gets very hot. Keep it out of traffic and away from furniture and drapes, and keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from it.
  • Supervise young children in the same room. If anyone at risk is in the house, a child guard or an adjustable safety gate is recommended.
  • The barrier screen that comes with the stove reduces burns from the hot glass and must be in place. If it's damaged, replace it with Jøtul's barrier for this stove (part 157713). Put back any screen removed for service before using the stove.
  • Burn natural gas or propane only, never wood, cardboard, paper or coal.
  • Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors or liquids near the stove.
  • Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the stove and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

If you smell gas

  • Don't light any appliance. Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the stove.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty is for the original retail purchaser, counted from the date of purchase:

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas and electrical parts: controls, plumbing, valve, blower1 year

Not covered

  • Parts that wear with normal use, including gaskets and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress)
  • Installation that doesn't follow the instructions or local codes
  • Unauthorized modification, use or repair
  • Enamel damage from misuse (bubbling, cracking or discoloration)
  • Travel time, loss of service, and damage in transit
Report problems within 60 days. Jøtul must receive notice of a possible defect within sixty days of the date it was first discovered, or reasonably could have been. Contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer to start a claim.

The warranty is void if installation or service is done by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier. It isn't transferable. Keep your dated sales receipt. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specVent.title: Vertical & co-linear venting
specVent.html:
Vertical run8 ft. (2.43 m) min · 35 ft. (10.66 m) max
Co-linear height (Fig. 13)10 ft. (3.05 m) min · 35 ft. (10.66 m) max
Co-linear horizontal run / offset2 ft. (61 cm) max
Elbowsfour 45° or two 90°, not counting the 45° elbow on the stove
Cap discharge opening to roof18 in. min, horizontally
Vent to combustibles1" all sides
Firestopevery floor, framed 10" X 10" inside

Terminate within the shaded areas of the vent windows (pp. 10–11) and set the exhaust restrictor to match. Support offsets with wall straps at three-foot intervals; use 45° rather than 90° elbows where possible. Enclose venting exposed above the first floor. Steep roofs, nearby trees and wind can cause poor draft or down-draft; a taller vent may help.

Co-linear (p. 12): masonry chimney with a fireclay liner the entire length, or a UL 103 / ULC S-629 prefab chimney of 6 inches (150 mm) minimum inside diameter, cleaned and inspected first; dual 3" flex liners. The air intake flex must extend 6 feet beyond the damper area; if it doesn't run the full length, install a metal block-off plate sealing the flue from the room. Fig. 14: 25 1/2" to center of flue collar, 29" to top of the co-linear adapter; subtract 2 1/4" for short legs.

Note: the vertical termination list on p. 9, which also sets the 2 ft. co-linear horizontal limit, gives an 8 ft. minimum vertical run; Fig. 13 on p. 12 gives a 10 ft. minimum co-linear height.
The manual prints the cap-to-roof clearance as 18 in. (610 mm) on p. 9; the same page pairs 61 cm with 2 ft., and its Fig. 8 shows 18 min.

specHoriz.html:

Terminate within the shaded part of the vent window (Figs. 9 or 11). Never run the vent downward from stove to cap. Don't fill the wall air space with insulation. Use a vinyl siding standoff on vinyl siding, and don't recess the cap into a wall or siding.

The air inlet restrictor must be set fully open for any snorkel termination (Fig. 6, p. 9).

conflicts.issue: Elbow off the control valve to create blower clearance: 45° elbow (Gas Supply Connection, p. 17) vs 90° elbow (Optional Blower, p. 24).
Minimum vertical run 8 ft. (2.43 m) in the vertical termination list that also sets the co-linear horizontal limit (p. 9) vs 'Min. Co-linear Height - 10 ft. (3.05 m)' in Fig. 13 (p. 12).
Cap discharge-to-roof clearance printed as '18 in. (610 mm)' on p. 9; the same page equates 2 ft. with 61 cm, so the inch and metric values disagree.
Vent terminal clearance table rows E, F, G print '12 in,. (46 cm)'; rows A, B, C, J, M print 12 in. as (30 cm) and row D prints 18 in. as (46 cm).
Rating plate (which also carries the lighting instructions) is 'hung on the back' (p. 3) and 'attached to the back of the stove' (p. 22) vs 'attached the bottom of the stove' (p. 21).

review.notes: Physical pages equal the printed footer pages throughout, but the table of contents and many internal cross-references point one page late from p. 15 on (e.g. Gas Pressure 'page 19' is p. 18, Log Set 'page 21' is p. 20, parts list 'page 29' is p. 28, fig. 38 'page 22' is p. 21, air shutter 'page 20' is p. 19); the guide uses physical pages. Broken references: p. 6 sends barrier part numbers to 'fig. 72, page 34' (the manual has 32 pages) - the guide uses Safety Screen Barrier 157713 from the parts list (p. 28); p. 23 points to a maintenance-history form on page 30, which is blank; the fuel conversion procedure cites 'fig. 47, Illustrated Parts Breakdown' (the breakdown is Fig. 52, p. 27; Fig. 47 is the blower wiring diagram); p. 8 says to use 'the chart in Table 1' for exhaust restrictor positions, but no Table 1 exists - only the vent-window callouts on pp. 10-11 were used (NG co-linear B; LP straight vertical co-linear C; LP co-linear with max 2 ft. offset printed as lowercase 'a', shown as A). Not transcribed (diagrams or ambiguous text): vent termination windows Figs. 9-12 (labels are undecodable glyphs), dimension drawing p. 4, hearth protection Fig. 1 (14"/27" unlabeled), mantel/trim charts Figs. 4a-4c, horizontal vent Figs. 16-18, exhaust restrictor factory letter in Fig. 6/7 ('D'), and vent terminal table rows B, C, F, G, H, I, K, L whose Canada/U.S. column alignment is ambiguous in the extracted text (rows A, D, E, M, N have identical values in both columns; row J is on one line, Canada then U.S.). Blower install step 4 (p. 24) calls for '#7 x 1/2" screws' while the kit list (item 11) is '#8 x 1/2" phillips screw (2)'; not used in the guide. Scrambled-font text decoded with the 29-code-point rule: running headers on pp. 7, 10, 11, 17 ('137750_Rev_V GF 400 DV 10/21') and Fig. 25 'milot _ase' = 'Pilot Base'; the remaining glyph runs could not be decoded and were not used. French passages (pp. 5, 15) duplicate English text; the gas-smell block is in English (pp. 1, 31), so nothing was translated. Boilerplate calls the unit a 'fireplace insert' or 'fireplace' in places (pp. 2, 4, 23, 24); the cover and p. 3 call it a direct vent gas stove. Lighting step 7 says to 'repeat Steps 5 through 8' if the pilot goes out; kept as printed. Pressure-testing rule (p. 18) kept as printed: disconnect above 1/2 psig, isolate at or above 1/2 psig. The manual gives no heating area or weight, so catalog heating_area_sqft_max 2000 and weight_lb 260 are unverified; catalog height/width/depth (28.5/26.5/20.5) match values on the p. 4 drawing but those labels are unassigned. Catalog finish 'Linen' is not named in the manual's parts list (Matte Black Paint, Blue Black Enamel, Ivory Enamel, Jøtul Iron Paint, Jøtul Iron Enamel, Brown Majolica Enamel, Blue Majolica Enamel), and the manual doesn't describe open-door viewing.
